notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.28_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.28.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.28.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Added

- **The tray icon says when you are away.** The same mask, in the same place
  at the same size, with its unlit half fallen into shadow — a face half gone
  into the dark, which reads as somebody who has stepped away from the room
  without a badge or a colour code anybody has to learn. It follows the status
  itself, so the half hour that sets you to Away is the half hour that dims
  the icon, and coming back to the keyboard brings it up again.

  A call outranks it: if you are somehow in one while away, the icon keeps the
  green dot that says the microphone is open.

- **Unread is a bar on the rail's edge, and the red count means somebody is
  talking to you.** The two were the same mark before: one red number for
  anything at all, hidden the moment you opened the server it belonged to. Now
  the bar at the edge says there is something here you have not read — longer
  when there is more of it — and the red count is kept for replies with your
  name on them. Both stay visible for the server you are already in, because a
  server is many channels and the one on screen is not the only one that fills
  up.

  The dot in front of the server's name is gone with it. It said whether that
  server had anybody connected, which is what the light on the same server's
  icon in the rail, two inches to its left, was already saying.

- **The three checkboxes that are still checkboxes are drawn properly.** A
  browser's own tick, tinted with the accent colour, fills its box corner to
  corner and reads as clipped — the one place a mark should not stop is
  exactly where its container does. These are drawn instead: a small outlined
  box with a tick half again its size, hung off the top-right corner so the
  mark sits *on* the box rather than being squeezed into it. The mark is the accent colour rather
  than white on a filled box, which is what lets it cross the edge and stay
  visible on a light panel as well as a dark one.

- **Settings are switches now, not checkboxes.** A checkbox is a thing you
  tick and then submit; every one of these took effect the moment it was
  pressed, which is what a switch is for — and screen readers say so too, "on"
  rather than "checked". The whole line is the target rather than a small
  square at the end of it, and the ones that cannot be operated dim themselves
  instead of relying on the group around them to look faded.

  The three that really are form fields — the two on "Create a channel" and
  the one on an invite — stay checkboxes, because they are answered as part of
  filling something in rather than acted on where they stand.

- **The app icon can take your accent colour.** Off by default — the mask has
  a colour of its own, and it is what you pick Ruze out by in a panel of
  twenty icons — but "Draw the app icon in it too", under the accent swatches,
  hands the icon whichever of the eleven colours the rest of the app is using.

  The shading is kept exactly as drawn and only the hue is replaced, so the
  face still reads as a face rather than a flat silhouette; a grey accent
  drains it to grey rather than tinting it, because that is what picking grey
  means. The one thing that never changes colour is the dot that says you are
  in a call: a signal that moved with a preference would stop being one.

### Fixed

- **A chime no longer swallows an unrelated one.** Sounds were held apart by
  a single clock, so somebody walking into your voice channel a fifth of a
  second after a message arrived went unannounced. The gap is kept per kind
  now: a flood of messages still throttles messages, and nothing else.

- **Dropdowns in the light theme were drawn dark.** A window set to light on a
  desktop set to dark got the desktop's answer for anything the app had not
  drawn itself — so every dropdown came out black-on-white's opposite, in the
  one panel that was white. The app's own theme decides that now, the same
  attribute everything else here follows, which also settles the popup list a
  dropdown opens, the scrollbars and every other control the platform draws.

  The closed dropdown is drawn here rather than by the platform besides: GTK,
  WebView2 and Android each have their own idea of the shape and metrics of a
  select, and it was the one control in the app that looked borrowed from
  somewhere else.

### Changed

- **A wider mask, so the icon carries in a system tray.** A panel fits a square
  icon by its height, which means height is spent for you and width is the only
  room left — and the mark used 93% of the square top to bottom against 62%
  side to side. That third of the slot standing empty down each side is the
  whole of why it looked small beside its neighbours. The skull is broader now,
  filling three quarters of the width, and the same widening is on the Android
  launcher artwork so the face does not differ between the tray and the phone.
